key_insight: Explainable deep reinforcement learning can optimize residential building energy management while making battery-control decisions more transparent and trustworthy.
engineering_relevance: The framework helps lower electricity costs and improve operational control for buildings with PV, storage, dynamic tariffs, and weather-dependent loads.
method: Trained on-policy and off-policy DRL agents on an expanded state space with demand, PV, battery, SoC, tariffs, weather, calendar, holiday, and forecast inputs.
Compared A2C and PPO against off-policy methods for building energy management.
Applied post-hoc explanation methods to interpret learned policies and decision behavior.
evidence_signal: Experiments on both synthetic data and real-world LLEC data showed on-policy methods, especially A2C and PPO, achieved better cumulative rewards and more stable policies.
watch_item: Results may depend on forecast quality, data availability, and how well the learned policy generalizes from the tested building context to other sites.
paper_title: Explainable Data-driven Deep Reinforcement Learning Methods for Optimal Energy Management in Buildings
